analysis.title: GS Blekos - Marketcolour 6 Nov 2026
key_insights: US equities sold off sharply on 11/5: S&P 500 -436bps to 7353, Russell 2000 -455bps to 2729, Nasdaq 100 -636bps to 26629. S&P 500 and Russell 2000 had their worst sessions since April 2025, and the Nasdaq its worst day since March 2020.
VIX rose 70% to 28.15. All sectors fell: Tech -7.30%, Industrials -4.12%, Staples -0.67%. The Nasdaq VIX had its biggest one-day move since Covid.
Nvidia (-9.26%) accounted for 11.41% of the NDX move and Micron (-17.46%) for 11.06%. The GS AI Semis basket fell 12.16% and the Data Centers basket fell 12.03%.

Supply in semis/AI continued, but the demand seen the prior day in hyperscalers/Mag 7 did not return. The desk saw no offsetting bid for hyperscalers or defensive tech, which had helped support the index the day before.

Flow: floor inbounds were a 10 out of 10 but overall activity was a 5 out of 10. High-touch activity was much quieter than Wednesday. The desk attributes price action to top-down pressure through macro instruments, with ETFs about 32% of the tape.
Asset managers were net sellers, driven by steady supply across semis/AI. Hedge fund flows were roughly balanced while short books were toggled aggressively.

Global fundamental long/short hedge funds fell 1.3% (a -2 SD move), mainly on market/beta exposure, and are +8.7% YTD. TMT funds fell more than 4% and are roughly flat to slightly positive YTD, down from about +24% before the June/July AI sell-off.
US-focused funds fell 1.7% (+5.5% YTD). Systematic long/short managers rose 0.2% (+16% YTD). Multi-strats fell 1.4%, with Momentum down 3.7 SD.

GS estimates October nonfarm payrolls at +75k vs consensus +65k and a three-month average of +51k, citing low layoffs and a solid big-data signal. It forecasts average hourly earnings +0.3% m/m and unemployment unchanged at 4.2%, both in line with consensus.

GS cut its end-2026 gold forecast to $4,150/toz and its end-2027 forecast to $4,800/toz from $5,400, citing the Fed's hawkish shift for positioning. It keeps a constructive long-term view on central bank demand of 60 tonnes/month through 2026-27, vs 17 tonnes/month before 2022.
Airbnb said about 40% of Q3 2026 customer support issues were resolved without a human agent, and support cost per booking fell more than 17% y/y.

GS downgraded Kuehne + Nagel to Neutral. The analyst expects the container market to cool in FY27 and sees cyclical margin mean reversion as now more consensual. Near term, GSe Q4 EBIT is 3% above VA consensus, but FY28 EBIT is under 2% ahead.

IAG 3Q26 EBIT was EUR1.73bn, 5% below company consensus of EUR1.81bn, partly from extra disruption costs. Passenger revenue missed on lower volume. RASK was +4%, in line, with N Atlantic +11.5% vs GS 9% and Asia 3.4% vs 13%.
Daimler Truck Q4 EBIT was 1% ahead, with help from FX and tariff reimbursement. Orders missed by 9%. FY26 guidance was maintained.
Amadeus Q3 was in line, with FCF EUR564.2mn vs consensus EUR532.6mn. Operating income was EUR506.7mn vs consensus EUR521.7mn. Guidance was reiterated at the low end of mid-to-high single digit.
NDX is re-testing its multi-year base trendline. Semis have underperformed the market by more than 15 points over 5 days, the biggest such stretch since 2002.
